safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states the patient denies throat closing sensation; generated facts do not mention throat closing/denial.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In a suspected allergic reaction/anaphylaxis evaluation, documenting absence of “throat closing” helps risk-stratify airway involvement; omitting this negative finding can lead to ambiguity and potentially unnecessary escalation or miscommunication across handoffs. In this case, escalation was already recommended, so the incremental harm is limited but not zero.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states penicillin allergy; generated allergies section is empty and does not mention penicillin.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document a penicillin allergy can lead to inadvertent prescribing/administration of a contraindicated antibiotic, risking a serious allergic reaction including anaphylaxis. Allergy documentation errors are high-risk because they can directly precipitate preventable severe harm.
